Polemic ( / p ə ˈ l ɛ m ɪ k / pə- LEHM -ick , US also /- ˈ l i m ɪ k / -⁠LEEM-ick ) is contentious rhetoric intended to support a specific position by forthright claims and to undermine the opposing position. The practice of such argumentation is called polemics , which are seen in arguments on controversial topics. A person who writes polemics, or speaks polemically, is called a polemicist . [ 1 ] The word derives from Ancient Greek πολεμικός ( polemikos ) ' warlike, hostile ' , [ 1 ] [ 2 ] from πόλεμος ( polemos ) ' war ' . [ 3 ]
